decisions.reason: The consumer superfood drink mix sits outside the firm's announced core of waste-to-value technology, took little investment and carries no visible public commitment, so dropping it writes off little and needs no justification.

The modular plant extensions are part of the firm's central waste-to-energy platform, so they are kept as part of the course already invested in, even though they were only mentioned rather than featured.

WASTX Oil was launched with a dated public press release, had its own page and is central to the firm's announced direction, so heavy sunk investment and public commitment favour keeping it and blaming weak results on temporary market causes.

The plastic-waste-to-fuel plant was raised to its own page in 2019 and fits the firm's flagship WASTX technology line, so its engineering investment and visible commitment argue for persisting with it.
